metadata.title: A Kähler Structure on Cartan Spaces

extraction_notes.note: Sections 4.1-4.2 derive the Levi-Civita connection and the curvature components in running text with no stated result or proof environment; each numbered display is an equation node and the 'from (a) and (b) we obtain' links are hand-added uses edges between equations.

Two different equations (30) and (31) carry the same label '8', so \ref{8} is ambiguous; also \label{th1} sits after \end{theorem}, so the proof of Theorem 3.3 was not linked by syntax and its proves edge was added by hand.

Proof of Theorem 4.1 has a long unlabelled forward direction before the Case labels; it was made a container step with children rather than one flat setup step, and the 'Conversely' paragraph is a separate setup step.

Standard background facts on Cartan spaces stated without citation: the existence/uniqueness of the canonical metrical connection is stated in full and kept as an external theorem, the smaller facts as external claims.
The prose after Theorem 3.4 argues that (27) implies constant scalar curvature; the argument was split from its concluding 'Hence we conclude ...' sentence, taken as the claim.
The Introduction restates the metric, J and the main theorems; these copies were not given nodes. The 'Recall ... P^j_{ik}' sentence opening Section 4.1 was left in prose.

metadata.extraction_comment: Theorem 4.3's forward direction is only asserted ('we have computed ... the result is zero') and its converse is proved only for Berwald-Cartan spaces, hence semi_formal.

nodes.name: Cotangent bundle and canonical coordinates
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional $C^{\infty}$ manifold and $\pi^{\ast}:T^{\ast}M\rightarrow M$ its cotangent bundle. If $(x^i)$ are local coordinates on $M$, then $(x^i,p_i)$ will be taken as local coordinates on $T^{\ast}M$ with the momenta $(p_i)$ provided by $p=p_idx^i$ where $p\in T^{\ast}_xM$, $x=(x^i)$ and $(dx^i)$ is the natural basis of $T^{\ast}_xM$.
nodes.statement_short: Coordinates $(x^i,p_i)$ on the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of an $n$-manifold $M$, with momenta $p_i$.

nodes.name: Vertical subspace and vertical distribution
nodes.statement: The kernel $V_{(x,p)}$ of the differential $d\pi^{\ast}:T_{(x,p)}T^{\ast}M\rightarrow T_xM$ is called the vertical subspace of $T_{(x,p)}T^{\ast}M$ and the mapping $(x,p)\rightarrow V_{(x,p)}$ is a regular distribution on $T^{\ast}M$ called the vertical distribution.

nodes.name: Liouville vector field and Liouville 1-form
nodes.statement: The vector field $C^{\ast}=p_i\dot{\partial}^i$ is called the Liouville vector field and $\omega=p_idx^i$ is called the Liouville 1-form on $T^{\ast}M$.

nodes.name: Canonical symplectic structure
nodes.statement: Then $d\omega$ is the canonical symplectic structure on $T^{\ast}M$.

nodes.name: Horizontal distribution
nodes.statement: For an easer handling of the geometrical objects on $T^{\ast}M$ it is usual to consider a supplementary distribution to the vertical distribution, $(x,p)\rightarrow N_{(x,p)}$, called the horizontal distribution and to report all geometrical objects on $T^{\ast}M$ to the decomposition \begin{equation} T_{(x,p)}T^{\ast}M=N_{(x,p)}\oplus V_{(x,p)}. \end{equation}
nodes.genus: supplementary distribution to the vertical distribution

nodes.name: d-geometrical objects
nodes.statement: The pieces produced by the decomposition (\ref{decom}) are called \textit{d}-geometrical objects (\textit{d} is for distinguished) since their local components behave like geometrical objects on $M$, although they depend on $x=(x^i)$ and momenta $p=(p_i)$.

nodes.name: Adapted horizontal frame
nodes.statement: The horizontal distribution is taken as being locally spanned by the local vector fields \begin{equation} \delta_i:=\partial_i+N_{ij}(x,p)\dot{\partial}^j. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Nonlinear connection
nodes.statement: The horizontal distribution is called also a nonlinear connection on $T^{\ast}M$ and the functions $(N_{ij})$ are called the local coefficients of this nonlinear connection.

nodes.name: Symmetry of the nonlinear connection of a regular Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: It is important to note that any regular Hamiltonian on $T^{\ast}M$ determines a nonlinear connection whose local coefficients verify $N_{ij}=N_{ji}$.
conclusions: determines a nonlinear connection whose local coefficients verify $N_{ij}=N_{ji}$

nodes.name: Dual adapted coframe
nodes.statement: The dual of it is $(dx^i,\delta P_i)$, for $\delta p_i=dp_i-N_{ji}dx^j$.

nodes.name: Cartan structure
nodes.statement: A Cartan structure on $M$ is a function $K:T^{\ast}M\longrightarrow [0,\infty)$ which has the following properties: (i) $K$ is $C^{\infty}$ on $T^{\ast}M_0=T^{\ast}M-\{0\}$; (ii) $K(x,\lambda p)=\lambda K(x,p)$ for all $\lambda>0$ and (iii) the $n\times n$ matrix $(g^{ij})$, where $g^{ij}(x,p)=\frac{1}{2}\dot{\partial}^i\dot{\partial}^jK^2(x,p)$, is positive definite at all points of $T^{\ast}M_0$.
differentia: the $n\times n$ matrix $(g^{ij})$, where $g^{ij}(x,p)=\frac{1}{2}\dot{\partial}^i\dot{\partial}^jK^2(x,p)$, is positive definite at all  points of $T^{\ast}M_0$
nodes.statement_short: A Cartan structure is a fibrewise 1-homogeneous function $K$ on $T^*M$, smooth off the zero section, whose fibre Hessian of $K^2$ is positive definite.

nodes.name: Cartan space
nodes.statement: The pair $(M,K)$ is called a Cartan space.

nodes.name: Momentum p^i and Cartan tensor C^{ijk}
nodes.statement: Using this notations, let us define \[ p^i=\frac{1}{2}\dot{\partial}^iK^2\ \ \textrm{and}\ \ C^{ijk}=-\frac{1}{4}\dot{\partial}^i\dot{\partial}^j\dot{\partial}^kK^2. \]

nodes.name: Formal Christoffel symbols
nodes.statement: One considers the formal Christoffel symbols by \begin{equation} \gamma^i_{jk}(x,p):=\frac{1}{2}g^{is}(\partial_kg_{js}+\partial_jg_{sk}-\partial_sg_{jk}), \end{equation} and the contractions $\gamma^{\circ}_{jk}(x,p):=\gamma^i_{jk}(x,p)p_i$, $\gamma^{\circ}_{j\circ}:=\gamma^i_{jk}p_ip^k$.

nodes.name: Miron's canonical nonlinear connection
nodes.statement: Then the functions \begin{equation} N_{ij}(x,p)=\gamma^{\circ}_{ij}(x,p)-\frac{1}{2}\gamma^{\circ}_{h\circ}(x,p)\dot{\partial}^hg_{ij}(x,p), \end{equation} define a nonlinear connection on $T^{\ast}M$.
nodes.statement_short: The canonical nonlinear connection of a Cartan space, built from the formal Christoffel symbols.

nodes.name: N-linear connection
nodes.statement: A linear connection $D$ on $T^{\ast}M$ is said to be an $N$-linear connection if $D$ preserves by parallelism the distribution $N$ and $V$, also we have $D\theta=0$, for $\theta=\delta p_i\wedge dx^i$.
differentia: $D$ preserves by parallelism the distribution $N$ and $V$

nodes.name: Local form of an N-linear connection
nodes.statement: One proves that an $N$-linear connection can be represented in the adapted basis $(\delta_i,\dot{\partial}^i)$ in the form \begin{eqnarray} D_{\delta_j}\delta_i\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!H^k_{ij}\delta_j,\ \ \ D_{\delta_j}\dot{\partial}^i=-H^i_{kj}\dot{\partial}^k,\\ D_{\dot{\partial}^j}\delta_i\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!V^{kj}_i\delta_k,\ \ \ D_{\dot{\partial}^j}\dot{\partial}^i=-V^{ij}_k\dot{\partial}^k, \end{eqnarray} where $V^{kj}_i$ is a \textit{d}-tensor field and $H^k_{ij}(x,p)$ behave like the coefficients of a linear connection on $M$.
conclusions: an $N$-linear connection can be represented in the adapted basis $(\delta_i,\dot{\partial}^i)$ in the form

nodes.name: h- and v-covariant derivatives
nodes.statement: The functions $H^k_{ij}$ and $V^{kj}_i$ define operators of \textit{h}-covariant and \textit{v}-covariant derivatives in the algebra of \textit{d}-tensor fields, denoted by $_{|k}$ and $\mid^k$, respectively. For $g^{ij}$ these are given by \begin{eqnarray} {g^{ij}}_{|k}\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!\delta_kg^{ij}+g^{sj}H^i_{sk}+g^{is}H^j_{sk},\\ g^{ij}\!\!\mid^k\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!\dot{\partial}^kg^{ij}+g^{sj}V^{ik}_s+g^{is}V^{jk}_s. \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Metrical N-linear connection
nodes.statement: An \textit{N}-linear connection given in the adapted basis $(\delta_i,\dot{\partial}^j)$ as $D\Gamma(N)=(H^i_{jk},V^{ik}_j)$ is called metrical if \begin{equation} {g^{ij}}_{|k}=0,\ \ \ \ g^{ij}\!\!\mid^k=0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of the canonical metrical connection
nodes.statement: One verifies that the \textit{N}-linear connection $C\Gamma(N)=(H^i_{jk},C^{ik}_j)$ with \begin{eqnarray} H^i_{jk}\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!\frac{1}{2}g^{is}(\delta_jg_{sk}+\delta_kg_{js}-\delta_sg_{jk}),\\ C^{jk}_i\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!-\frac{1}{2}g_{is}(\dot{\partial}^jg^{sk}+\dot{\partial}^kg^{sj}-\dot{\partial}^sg^{jk})=g_{is}C^{sjk}, \end{eqnarray} is metrical and its \textit{h}-torsion $T^i_{jk}:=H^i_{jk}-H^i_{kj}=0$, \textit{v}-torsion $S^{jk}_i:=C^{jk}_i-C^{kj}_i=0$ and deflection tensor $\Delta_{ij}=N_{ij}-p_kH^k_{ij}=0$. Moreover, it is unique with these properties.
conclusions: is metrical and its \textit{h}-torsion $T^i_{jk}:=H^i_{jk}-H^i_{kj}=0$, \textit{v}-torsion $S^{jk}_i:=C^{jk}_i-C^{kj}_i=0$ and deflection tensor $\Delta_{ij}=N_{ij}-p_kH^k_{ij}=0$
Moreover, it is unique with these properties.
nodes.statement_short: The N-linear connection $C\Gamma(N)$ is the unique metrical one with vanishing h-torsion, v-torsion and deflection.

nodes.name: Canonical metrical connection
nodes.statement: This is called the canonical metrical connection of the Cartan space $(M,K)$.

nodes.name: Properties of the canonical metrical connection
nodes.statement: It has also the following properties: \begin{eqnarray} K^2_{|j}:\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!\delta_jK^2=0,\ \ K^2\!\!\mid^j=2p^j,\\ p_{i|j}\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\! p^i_{|j}=0,\ \ p_i\!\!\mid^j=\delta^j_i,\ \ p^i\!\!\mid^j=g^{ij}. \\ R_{kij}p^k\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!0, \ \ P^i_{jk}p^j=0,\ \ P^i_{jk}:=H^i_{jk}-{\dot{\partial}}^iN_{jk}. \\ \delta_ig_{jk}\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!H^s_{ji}g_{sk}+H^s_{ki}g_{js}. \end{eqnarray}
conclusions: It has also the following properties:
nodes.statement_short: Covariant derivatives of $K^2$, $p_i$, $p^i$ and identities for $R_{kij}$, $P^i_{jk}$ and $\delta_i g_{jk}$ under the canonical connection.

nodes.name: tau, v, alpha, beta
nodes.statement: Suppose that \begin{equation} \tau :=\frac{1}{2}K^2=\frac{1}{2}g^{ij}(x,p)p_{i}p_{j}, \end{equation} we consider a real valued smooth function $v$ defined on $[0,\infty)\subset {\mathbb R} $ and real constants $\alpha $ and $\beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Set $\tau=K^2/2$ and fix a smooth function $v$ on $[0,\infty)$ and real constants $\alpha,\beta$.

nodes.name: Tensor field G_{ij}
nodes.statement: We define the following symmetric $M$-tensor field of type (0,2) on $T^{\ast}M_0$ having the components \begin{equation} G_{ij}:=\frac{1}{\beta}g_{ij}+\frac{v(\tau )}{\alpha \beta }p_{i} p_{j}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Positive definiteness criterion for G_{ij}
nodes.statement: It follows easily that the matrix $(G_{ij})$ is positive definite if and only if $\alpha ,\beta >0,\, \, \,\, \alpha +2\tau v>0.$
conclusions: the matrix  $(G_{ij})$ is positive definite if and only if  $\alpha ,\beta >0,\, \, \,\, \alpha +2\tau v>0.$

nodes.name: Inverse components G^{kl}
nodes.statement: The inverse of this matrix has the entries \begin{equation} G^{kl}=\beta g^{kl}-\frac{v\beta }{\alpha +2\tau v}p^{k} p^{l}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Positive definiteness of G^{kl}
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that if the matrix $(G_{ij} )$ is positive definite, then matrix $(G^{kl} )$ is positive definite too.
conclusions: matrix $(G^{kl} )$ is positive definite too

nodes.name: Riemannian metric G on T^*M_0
nodes.statement: Using $(G_{ij})$ and $(G^{ij})$, the following Riemannian metric on $T^{\ast}M_0$ is defined \begin{equation} G=G_{ij}dx^{i}dx^{j}+G^{ij}\delta p_{i}\delta p_{j}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Almost complex structure J
nodes.statement: Now, we define an almost complex structure $J$ on $T^{\ast}M_0$ by \begin{equation} J(\delta _{i})=G_{ik}\dot{\partial}^k,\ \ \ J(\dot{\partial}^i)=-G^{ik}\delta _k. \end{equation}

nodes.name: J squares to minus identity
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that $J^2=-I$.

nodes.name: Almost Kahler structure on T^*M_0
conclusions: $(T^{\ast}M_0,G,J)$ is an almost K\"{a}hlerian manifold.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: Since the matrix $(H^{kl} )$ is the inverse of the matrix $(G_{ij} ),$ then we have \[ G(J\delta_i,J\delta_j)=G_{ik}G_{jr}G(\dot{\partial}^k,\dot{\partial}^r)=G_{ik}G_{jr}G^{kr}=G_{ij}=G(\delta_i,\delta_j). \] The relations \[ G(J\dot{\partial}^i,J\dot{\partial}^j)=G(\dot{\partial}^i,\dot{\partial}^j),\ \ \ \ G(J\delta _i,J\dot{\partial}^j)=G(\delta _i,\dot{\partial}^j)=0, \] may be obtained in a similar way, thus \[ G(JX,JY)=G(X,Y),\, \, \, \, \, \, \, \forall X,Y\in \Gamma(T^{\ast}M_0). \] This means that $G$ is almost Hermitian with respect to $J$. The fundamental 2-form associated by this almost K\"{a}hler structure is $\Omega$, defined by \[ \theta(X,Y):=G(X,JY),\, \, \, \, \forall X,Y\in \Gamma (T^{\ast}M_0). \] Then we get \[ \theta(\dot{\partial}^i,\delta_j)=G(\dot{\partial}^i,J\delta_j)=G(\dot{\partial}^i,G_{jk}\dot{\partial}^k)=G^{ik}G_{jk}=\delta^i_j, \] and \[ \theta(\delta_i,\delta_j)=\theta(\dot{\partial}^i,\dot{\partial}^j)=0. \] Hence, we have \begin{equation} \theta=\delta p_i\wedge dx^i, \end{equation} that is the canonical symplectic form of $T^{\ast}M$.
nodes.statement_short: Check $G(JX,JY)=G(X,Y)$ on the adapted frame, then compute the fundamental 2-form and identify it with the canonical symplectic form $\delta p_i\wedge dx^i$.

nodes.name: J preserves G on horizontal fields
nodes.statement: Since the matrix $(H^{kl} )$ is the inverse of the matrix $(G_{ij} ),$ then we have \[ G(J\delta_i,J\delta_j)=G_{ik}G_{jr}G(\dot{\partial}^k,\dot{\partial}^r)=G_{ik}G_{jr}G^{kr}=G_{ij}=G(\delta_i,\delta_j). \]

nodes.name: G is almost Hermitian
nodes.statement: The relations \[ G(J\dot{\partial}^i,J\dot{\partial}^j)=G(\dot{\partial}^i,\dot{\partial}^j),\ \ \ \ G(J\delta _i,J\dot{\partial}^j)=G(\delta _i,\dot{\partial}^j)=0, \] may be obtained in a similar way, thus \[ G(JX,JY)=G(X,Y),\, \, \, \, \, \, \, \forall X,Y\in \Gamma(T^{\ast}M_0). \] This means that $G$ is almost Hermitian with respect to $J$.
nodes.statement_short: The other frame pairings follow similarly, so $G(JX,JY)=G(X,Y)$: $G$ is almost Hermitian.

nodes.name: Fundamental 2-form
nodes.statement: The fundamental 2-form associated by this almost K\"{a}hler structure is $\Omega$, defined by \[ \theta(X,Y):=G(X,JY),\, \, \, \, \forall X,Y\in \Gamma (T^{\ast}M_0). \]

nodes.name: theta is the canonical symplectic form
nodes.statement: Hence, we have \begin{equation} \theta=\delta p_i\wedge dx^i, \end{equation} that is the canonical symplectic form of $T^{\ast}M$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $\theta=\delta p_i\wedge dx^i$, the canonical symplectic form.

nodes.name: Brackets of the adapted frame
nodes.statement: \rm{(\cite{MirHri}\cite{PT})} Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space. Then we have the following:\\ $(1)\ \ [\delta_i,\delta_j]=R_{kij}{\dot{\partial}}^k$,\\ $(2)\ \ [\delta_i,{\dot{\partial}}^j]=-({\dot{\partial}}^jN_{ik}){\dot{\partial}}^k$,\\ $(3)\ \ [{\dot{\partial}}^i,{\dot{\partial}}^j]=0$,\\ where $R_{kij}=\delta_jN_{ki}-\delta_iN_{kj}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Miron, Hrimiuc, Shimada, Sabau 2000; Peyghan & Tayebi
conclusions: $(1)\ \ [\delta_i,\delta_j]=R_{kij}{\dot{\partial}}^k$
$(2)\ \ [\delta_i,{\dot{\partial}}^j]=-({\dot{\partial}}^jN_{ik}){\dot{\partial}}^k$
$(3)\ \ [{\dot{\partial}}^i,{\dot{\partial}}^j]=0$
nodes.statement_short: Lie brackets of the adapted frame $(\delta_i,\dot\partial^i)$ on a Cartan space.

nodes.name: Integrability criterion for J
nodes.statement: Let $(M, K)$ be a Cartan space. Then $J$ is a complex structure on $T^{\ast}M_0$ if and only if $A_{kij}=0$ and \begin{equation} R_{kij}=\frac{v}{\alpha\beta^2}(g_{ik}p_j-g_{jk}p_i), \end{equation} where $A_{kij}=\delta_i G_{jk}-\delta_j G_{ik}+G_{ir}{\dot{\partial}}^rN_{jk}-G_{jr}{\dot{\partial}}^rN_{ik}$.
assumptions: Let $(M, K)$ be a Cartan space.
conclusions: $J$ is a complex structure on $T^{\ast}M_0$ if and only if $A_{kij}=0$ and

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: Using the definition of the Nijenhuis tensor field $N_J$ of $J$, that is, \[ N_J(X,Y)=[JX,JY]-J[JX,Y]-J[X,JY]-[X,Y],\ \ \ \forall X, Y\in \Gamma(T^{\ast}M) \] we get \begin{equation} N_J(\delta_i,\delta_j)=A_{hij}H^{hk}\delta_k+ (B_{kij}-R_{kij}){\dot{\partial}}^k, \end{equation} where $B_{kij}=G_{ir}{\dot{\partial}}^rG_{jk}-G_{jr}{\dot{\partial}}^rG_{ik}$. Let $C_{jk}^r:=g_{jl}g_{sk}C^{rls}$, then we have \[ {\dot{\partial}}^rg_{jk}=-g_{jl}g_{sk}{\dot{\partial}}^rg^{ls}=2g_{jl}g_{sk}C^{rls}=2C_{jk}^r. \] By the above equation, we obtain \begin{equation} G_{ir}{\dot{\partial}}^rG_{jk}=\frac{2}{\beta^2}C_{ijk} +\frac{v}{\alpha\beta^2}(g_{ji}p_k+g_{ik}p_j) +(\frac{v^{\prime}}{\alpha\beta^2}+\frac{2vv^{\prime}\tau}{\alpha\beta}+\frac{2v^2}{\alpha^2\beta^2})p_ip_jp_k. \end{equation} where $C_{ijk}=g_{ir}C_{jk}^r$. From (\ref{Nij2}) we get \begin{equation} B_{kij}=\frac{v}{\alpha\beta^2}(g_{ik}p_j-g_{jk}p_i). \end{equation} By a straightforward computation, it follows that $N_J({\dot{\partial}}^i,{\dot{\partial}}^j)=0, N_J({\dot{\partial}}^i,\delta_j)=0$, whenever $N_j(\delta_i,\delta_j)=0$. Therefore, from relations (\ref{Nij1}) and (\ref{Nij3}), we conclude that the necessary and sufficient conditions for vanishing the Nijenhuis tensor field $N_J$ is obtained, so that J is a complex structure. Thus $A_{kij}=0$ and (\ref{2}) hold.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the Nijenhuis tensor $N_J$ on the adapted frame via the bracket lemma; its vanishing gives exactly $A_{kij}=0$ and the stated form of $R_{kij}$.

nodes.name: Nijenhuis tensor on horizontal fields
nodes.statement: Using the definition of the Nijenhuis tensor field $N_J$ of $J$, that is, \[ N_J(X,Y)=[JX,JY]-J[JX,Y]-J[X,JY]-[X,Y],\ \ \ \forall X, Y\in \Gamma(T^{\ast}M) \] we get \begin{equation} N_J(\delta_i,\delta_j)=A_{hij}H^{hk}\delta_k+ (B_{kij}-R_{kij}){\dot{\partial}}^k, \end{equation} where $B_{kij}=G_{ir}{\dot{\partial}}^rG_{jk}-G_{jr}{\dot{\partial}}^rG_{ik}$.

nodes.name: Compute G_{ir} dot-partial^r G_{jk}
nodes.statement: By the above equation, we obtain \begin{equation} G_{ir}{\dot{\partial}}^rG_{jk}=\frac{2}{\beta^2}C_{ijk} +\frac{v}{\alpha\beta^2}(g_{ji}p_k+g_{ik}p_j) +(\frac{v^{\prime}}{\alpha\beta^2}+\frac{2vv^{\prime}\tau}{\alpha\beta}+\frac{2v^2}{\alpha^2\beta^2})p_ip_jp_k. \end{equation} where $C_{ijk}=g_{ir}C_{jk}^r$.

nodes.name: Compute B_{kij}
nodes.statement: From (\ref{Nij2}) we get \begin{equation} B_{kij}=\frac{v}{\alpha\beta^2}(g_{ik}p_j-g_{jk}p_i). \end{equation} By a straightforward computation, it follows that $N_J({\dot{\partial}}^i,{\dot{\partial}}^j)=0, N_J({\dot{\partial}}^i,\delta_j)=0$, whenever $N_j(\delta_i,\delta_j)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Derive $B_{kij}$; the other components of $N_J$ vanish when $N_J(\delta_i,\delta_j)=0$.

nodes.name: Conclude integrability conditions
nodes.statement: Therefore, from relations (\ref{Nij1}) and (\ref{Nij3}), we conclude that the necessary and sufficient conditions for vanishing the Nijenhuis tensor field $N_J$ is obtained, so that J is a complex structure. Thus $A_{kij}=0$ and (\ref{2}) hold.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing of $N_J$ is equivalent to $A_{kij}=0$ and (2).

nodes.name: Curvature constant c
nodes.statement: In equation (\ref{2}), we put $-\frac{v}{\alpha\beta^2}=c$, where $c$ is constant.

nodes.name: Integrability of J for n >= 3
nodes.statement: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space of dimension $n\geq 3$. Then the almost complex structure $J$ on $T^{\ast}M_0$ is integrable if and only if (\ref{3}) is hold and the function $v$ is given by \begin{equation} v=-c\alpha\beta^2. \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space of dimension $n\geq 3$.
conclusions: the almost complex structure $J$ on $T^{\ast}M_0$ is integrable if and only if (\ref{3}) is hold and the function $v$ is given by

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement: From equation $p_{i|k}=0$ of relation (\ref{4}), we conclude that $\delta_ip_k=N_{ik}$. Hence the tensor field $A_{kij}$ takes the form $A_{kij}=\delta_i g_{jk}-\delta_j g_{ik}+g_{ir}{\dot{\partial}}^rN_{jk}-g_{jr}{\dot{\partial}}^rN_{ik}$ and by part $(iii)$ of Proposition 2.3 in chapter 7 of \cite{MirHri}, it vanishes for Cartan spaces. Now we let $v=-c\alpha\beta^2$, then from equation $A_{kij}=0$ and Theorem \ref{3.3}, we conclude that $J$ is integrable if and only if (\ref{3}) is hold.
nodes.statement_short: Show $A_{kij}$ vanishes for Cartan spaces (via $p_{i|k}=0$ and Miron et al.), then apply Theorem 3.3 with $v=-c\alpha\beta^2$.

nodes.name: delta_i p_k = N_{ik}
nodes.statement: From equation $p_{i|k}=0$ of relation (\ref{4}), we conclude that $\delta_ip_k=N_{ik}$.

nodes.name: A_{kij} vanishes
nodes.statement: Hence the tensor field $A_{kij}$ takes the form $A_{kij}=\delta_i g_{jk}-\delta_j g_{ik}+g_{ir}{\dot{\partial}}^rN_{jk}-g_{jr}{\dot{\partial}}^rN_{ik}$ and by part $(iii)$ of Proposition 2.3 in chapter 7 of \cite{MirHri}, it vanishes for Cartan spaces.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $A_{kij}$ and invoke Miron et al. to see it vanishes.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: Now we let $v=-c\alpha\beta^2$, then from equation $A_{kij}=0$ and Theorem \ref{3.3}, we conclude that $J$ is integrable if and only if (\ref{3}) is hold.

nodes.name: Cartan space of constant scalar curvature
nodes.statement: A Cartan space $K^n$ is of constant scalar $c$ if \begin{equation} H_{hijk}p^ip^jX^hX^k=c(g_{hj}g_{ik}-g_{hk}g_{ij})p^ip^jX^hX^k, \end{equation} for every $(x,p)\in T^{\ast}_0M$ and $X=(X^i)\in T_xM$. Here $H_{hijk}$ is the (hh)h-curvature of the linear Cartan connection of $K^n$.
nodes.statement_short: $K^n$ has constant (scalar/flag) curvature $c$ if its (hh)h-curvature satisfies the constant-curvature identity on $p$ and arbitrary $X$.

nodes.name: Argument that (27) gives constant curvature
nodes.statement: We replace $H_{hijk}$ in (\ref{7}) with $g_{is}H^s_{hjk}$ and so it reduce to \begin{equation} p_sH^s_{hjk}p^jX^hX^k=c(p_hp_k-K^2g_{hk})X^hX^k. \end{equation} By part (ii) of Proposition 5.1 in chapter 7 of \cite{MirHri}, $p_sH^s_{hjk}=-R_{hjk}$, hence we get \[ R_{hjk}p^jX^hX^k=c(K^2g_{hk}-p_hp_k)X^hX^k, \] or equivalently \begin{equation} R_{hjk}p^j=c(K^2g_{hk}-p_hp_k), \end{equation} because $(X^h)$ and $X^k$ are arbitrary vector fields on $M$. It is easy to check that (\ref{8}) follows from (\ref{3}).
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the constant-curvature condition via $p_sH^s_{hjk}=-R_{hjk}$ as $R_{hjk}p^j=c(K^2g_{hk}-p_hp_k)$, which follows from (27).

nodes.name: Lower index
nodes.statement: We replace $H_{hijk}$ in (\ref{7}) with $g_{is}H^s_{hjk}$ and so it reduce to \begin{equation} p_sH^s_{hjk}p^jX^hX^k=c(p_hp_k-K^2g_{hk})X^hX^k. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Express via R_{hjk}
nodes.statement: By part (ii) of Proposition 5.1 in chapter 7 of \cite{MirHri}, $p_sH^s_{hjk}=-R_{hjk}$, hence we get \[ R_{hjk}p^jX^hX^k=c(K^2g_{hk}-p_hp_k)X^hX^k, \] or equivalently \begin{equation} R_{hjk}p^j=c(K^2g_{hk}-p_hp_k), \end{equation} because $(X^h)$ and $X^k$ are arbitrary vector fields on $M$.

nodes.name: Follows from (27)
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that (\ref{8}) follows from (\ref{3}).

nodes.name: Integrable case has constant scalar curvature
nodes.statement: Hence we conclude that if (\ref{3}) is hold, then Cartan space $K^n$ has the constant scalar curvature $c$.
conclusions: Cartan space $K^n$ has the constant scalar curvature $c$

nodes.name: Kahler structure on T^*M_0 and on the tube
nodes.statement: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space with constant flag curvature $c$. Suppose that $v$ is given by (\ref{constant}). Then\\ $(i)$ for negative constant $c$, structure $(T^{\ast}M_0,G,J)$ is a K\"{a}hler manifold;\\ $(ii)$ for positive constant $c$, the tube around the zero section in $T^{\ast}M$, defined by the condition $2\tau=K^2<\frac{1}{c\beta^2}$, is a K\"{a}hler manifold.
assumptions: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space with constant flag curvature $c$.
conclusions: $(i)$ for negative constant $c$, structure $(T^{\ast}M_0,G,J)$ is a K\"{a}hler manifold;
$(ii)$ for positive constant $c$, the tube around the zero section in $T^{\ast}M$, defined by the condition $2\tau=K^2<\frac{1}{c\beta^2}$,  is a K\"{a}hler manifold.
nodes.statement_short: For constant flag curvature $c$ and $v=-c\alpha\beta^2$: $T^*M_0$ is Kähler if $c<0$, and the tube $K^2<1/(c\beta^2)$ is Kähler if $c>0$.
nodes.label: THM1

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.5
nodes.statement: The function $uv$ must satisfies in the following condition \begin{equation} \alpha +2\tau u=\alpha (1+2(-c)\beta ^{2} \tau )>0,\, \, \, \, \, \alpha ,\beta >0. \end{equation} By using the above relation and Theorem \ref{3.4}, we complete the proof.

nodes.name: Levi-Civita connection of G
nodes.statement:
Also the Levi-Civita connection $
abla$ of the Riemannian manifold $(T^{\ast}M_0,G)$ is obtained from the formula  egin{eqnarray} 2G({
abla }_{X} Y,Z)\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!X(G(Y,Z))+Y(G(X,Z))-Z(G(X,Y))
onumber\ \!\!\!\!&+&\!\!\!\!G([X,Y],Z)-G([X,Z],Y)-G([Y,Z],X),\, \, \, \, \,  orall X,Y,Z\in \Gamma(T^{\ast}M_0), \end{eqnarray} and is characterized by the conditions $
abla G=0$ and $T=0$, where $T$ is the torsion tensor of $
abla$.

nodes.name: Curvature of nabla
Kahler-Einstein characterization
nodes.statement: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space of constant curvature $c$ and the components of the metric $G$ are given by (\ref{Kahler}). Then the following are hold if and only if $(M,K)$ is reduce to a Riemannian space.\\ $(i)$ for $c<0$, $(T^{\ast}M_0,G,J)$ is a K\"{a}hler Einstein manifold.\\ $(ii)$ for $c>0$, $(T_{\beta}^{\ast}M_0,G,J)$ is a K\"{a}hler Einstein manifold, where $T_{\beta}^{\ast}M_0$ is the tube around the zero section in $TM$ defined by $2\tau<\frac{1}{c\beta^2}$.
assumptions: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space of constant curvature $c$ and the components of the metric $G$ are given by (\ref{Kahler}).
conclusions: the following are hold if and only if $(M,K)$ is reduce to a Riemannian space.
nodes.statement_short: The (tube in the) cotangent bundle with the Kähler metric is Kähler-Einstein iff the Cartan space is Riemannian.
nodes.label: THM2

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement_short: Forward: compute curvature components in the Riemannian case to get $Ric=cn\beta G$. Converse: contract $Ric(\dot\partial^j,\dot\partial^k)$ with $p_k$, splitting $\lambda=0$ (contradiction) and $\lambda\neq0$ (forcing $I^j=0$).

nodes.name: Forward direction: Einstein when Riemannian
nodes.statement_short: If the Cartan space is Riemannian, all Ricci components equal $cn\beta G$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of C and P
nodes.statement: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space. Then $C^{hi}_k$ and $P^h_{ik}$ are vanish and $H^i_{jk}$ is a function of $(x^h)$.
nodes.statement_short: In the Riemannian case $C$ and $P$ vanish and $H$ depends on $x$ only.

nodes.name: Constant curvature for R
nodes.statement: From Proposition 10.2 in chapter 4 of \cite{MirHri}, we have $R_{kji}=-p_hR^h_{kji}$. Then we get \begin{equation} p_hR^h_{kji}=c(g_{kj}\delta^h_i-g_{ki}\delta^h_j)p_h. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use $R_{kji}=-p_hR^h_{kji}$ (Miron et al.) for constant curvature.

nodes.name: Differentiate
nodes.statement: Differentiating (\ref{Ricc2}) with respect to $p_s$, taking $p=0$, yields \[ R^s_{kji}=c(g_{kj}\delta^s_i-g_{ki}\delta^s_j). \]

nodes.name: K(delta,delta)delta
nodes.statement: By putting above equation in (\ref{Ricc1}), it follows that \begin{eqnarray} K(\delta_i,\delta_j)\delta_k\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!c\beta[(\frac{1}{\beta}g_{kj}-c\beta p_kp_j)\delta^s_i-(\frac{1}{\beta}g_{ki}-c\beta\ p_kp_i)\delta^s_j]\delta_s\nonumber\\ \!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!c\beta(G_{kj}\delta^s_i-G_{ki}\delta^s_j)\delta_s. \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Ric(delta,delta)
Vertical curvatures
nodes.statement: Similarly from (\ref{Curvature6}) and (\ref{curvature13}), respectively, we have \begin{eqnarray} K({\dot{\partial}}^i,{\dot{\partial}}^j){\dot{\partial}}^k=c\beta(G^{jk}\delta^i_s-G^{ik}\delta^j_s){\dot{\partial}}^s, \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} K(\delta_i,{\dot{\partial}}^j){\dot{\partial}}^k=c\beta G^{ks}\delta^j_i\delta_s. \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Ric(dp,dp)
Mixed curvatures
nodes.statement: By (\ref{curvature13}) and (\ref{curvature15}),respectively, we have \begin{equation} K(\delta_i,\delta_j){\dot{\partial}}^k=(R^k_{sij}+c\beta R_{hij}G^{hk}p_s){\dot{\partial}}^s, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} K({\dot{\partial}}^i,\delta_j){\dot{\partial}}^k=-c\beta G^{ks}\delta^i_j\delta_s. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Ric(dp,delta)=0
nodes.statement: By attention to (\ref{Ricc4}) and (\ref{Ricc12}), one can obtains \begin{equation} Ric({\dot{\partial}}^j,\delta_k)=G^{ih}G(K(\delta_i,{\dot{\partial}}^j)\delta_k,\delta_h) +G_{ih}G(K({\dot{\partial}}^i,{\dot{\partial}}^j)\delta_k,{\dot{\partial}}^h)=0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Einstein
nodes.statement: From (\ref{Ricc5}), (\ref{Ricc8}), (\ref{Ricc11}) and (\ref{Ricc13}), we deduce that \[ Ric(X,Y)=cn\beta G(X,Y),\ \ \ \forall X, Y\in\chi(T^{\ast}M). \] This means that $(T^{\ast}M,G)$ is a Einstein manifold.

nodes.name: Converse setup
nodes.statement: Conversely, suppose that the conditions $(i), (ii)$ are hold. Then there exists a real constant $\lambda$ such that $Ric(X,Y)=\lambda G(X,Y)$. We consider the following cases:
nodes.statement_short: Assume Einstein with constant $\lambda$ and split on $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Case (1): Ricci flat
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case (1)}. If $\lambda=0$ (i.e., $(T^{\ast}M,G)$ is Ricci flat), then we have $Ric({\dot{\partial}}^j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=0$. By using (\ref{Curvature6}),(\ref{curvature13}) and definition of Ricci tensor, we obtain \begin{eqnarray} 0=p_kRic({\dot{\partial}}^j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=cn\beta p_kG^{jk}- p_kC^{jk,s}_s\!\!\!\!&+&\!\!\!\!\frac{\beta^2}{2}\delta_s(P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr})p_k +\frac{\beta^2}{2}\delta_s(P^k_{rl}g^{lj}g^{sr})p_k\nonumber\\ \!\!\!\!&+&\!\!\!\! \frac{\beta^2}{2}g^{ts}p_k(P^j_{mt}H^k_{sh}g^{mh}+P^h_{mt}H^k_{sh}g^{mj}). \end{eqnarray} Since $P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr}p_k=P^j_{rl}p^lg^{sr}=0$ and $\delta_sp_k=H^h_{sk}p_h$, then we have \begin{eqnarray*} \delta_s(P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr})p_k\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!-(\delta_sp_k)P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr}\\ \!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!-P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr}H^h_{sk}p_h. \end{eqnarray*} Replacing $h$ and $k$, changing $r$ to $t$, and $l$ to $m$ in the above equation yields \begin{equation} \delta_s(P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr})p_k=-P^j_{tm}g^{mh}g^{st}H^k_{sh}p_k. \end{equation} Similarly, we have \begin{equation} \delta_s(P^k_{rl}g^{lj}g^{sr})p_k=-P^h_{tm}g^{mj}g^{st}H^k_{sh}p_k. \end{equation} With direct computation, we get \begin{eqnarray} \nonumber cn\beta p_kG^{jk}\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!cn\beta p_k(\beta g^{jk}+\frac{c\beta^3}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}p^jp^k)\\ \!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!\frac{cn\beta^2}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}p^j, \end{eqnarray} and \begin{equation} p_kC^{jk,s}_s=-p^{,s}_kC^{jk}_s=-\delta^s_kC^{jk}_s=-C^{js}_s=-I^j. \end{equation} By using (\ref{Ricc14})-(\ref{Ricc18}), we obtain \begin{equation} \frac{cn\beta^2}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}p^j+I^j=0. \end{equation} Since $p_jI^j=0$, then by contracting (\ref{Ricc19}) with $p_j$, we have \begin{equation} \frac{2cn\beta^2\tau}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}=0. \end{equation} From the above equation, we conclude that $\beta=0$ and this is a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: If $\lambda=0$, contracting $Ric(\dot\partial^j,\dot\partial^k)$ with $p_k$ forces $\beta=0$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Open case lambda=0
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case (1)}. If $\lambda=0$ (i.e., $(T^{\ast}M,G)$ is Ricci flat), then we have $Ric({\dot{\partial}}^j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=0$.

nodes.name: Contract with p_k
nodes.statement: By using (\ref{Curvature6}),(\ref{curvature13}) and definition of Ricci tensor, we obtain \begin{eqnarray} 0=p_kRic({\dot{\partial}}^j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=cn\beta p_kG^{jk}- p_kC^{jk,s}_s\!\!\!\!&+&\!\!\!\!\frac{\beta^2}{2}\delta_s(P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr})p_k +\frac{\beta^2}{2}\delta_s(P^k_{rl}g^{lj}g^{sr})p_k\nonumber\\ \!\!\!\!&+&\!\!\!\! \frac{\beta^2}{2}g^{ts}p_k(P^j_{mt}H^k_{sh}g^{mh}+P^h_{mt}H^k_{sh}g^{mj}). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Contract with $p_k$ using the curvature formulas.

nodes.name: Relabel indices
nodes.statement: Replacing $h$ and $k$, changing $r$ to $t$, and $l$ to $m$ in the above equation yields \begin{equation} \delta_s(P^j_{rl}g^{lk}g^{sr})p_k=-P^j_{tm}g^{mh}g^{st}H^k_{sh}p_k. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Direct computations
nodes.statement: With direct computation, we get \begin{eqnarray} \nonumber cn\beta p_kG^{jk}\!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!cn\beta p_k(\beta g^{jk}+\frac{c\beta^3}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}p^jp^k)\\ \!\!\!\!&=&\!\!\!\!\frac{cn\beta^2}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}p^j, \end{eqnarray} and \begin{equation} p_kC^{jk,s}_s=-p^{,s}_kC^{jk}_s=-\delta^s_kC^{jk}_s=-C^{js}_s=-I^j. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Contract with p_j
nodes.statement: Since $p_jI^j=0$, then by contracting (\ref{Ricc19}) with $p_j$, we have \begin{equation} \frac{2cn\beta^2\tau}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}=0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: From the above equation, we conclude that $\beta=0$ and this is a contradiction.

nodes.name: Case (2): lambda nonzero
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case (2)}. If $\lambda\neq0$, then we have \[ p_kRic({\dot{\partial}}^j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=\lambda G^{jk}p_k. \] Therefore by using (\ref{Curvature6}), (\ref{curvature13}), (\ref{Ricc15})-(\ref{Ricc18}), we obtain \begin{equation} I^j=(\lambda-cn\beta)\frac{\beta}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}p^j. \end{equation} By contracting (\ref{Ricc21}) with $p_j$, we have \begin{equation} (\lambda-cn\beta)\frac{2\beta\tau}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}=0, \end{equation} i.e., $\lambda=cn\beta$. Then from (\ref{Ricc21}), we result that $I^j=0$, i.e., $(M,K)$ is reduce to a Riemannian space.
nodes.statement_short: If $\lambda\neq0$, contraction gives $\lambda=cn\beta$ and hence $I^j=0$: Riemannian.

nodes.name: Contract
nodes.statement: By contracting (\ref{Ricc21}) with $p_j$, we have \begin{equation} (\lambda-cn\beta)\frac{2\beta\tau}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}=0, \end{equation} i.e., $\lambda=cn\beta$.

nodes.name: Riemannian
nodes.statement: Then from (\ref{Ricc21}), we result that $I^j=0$, i.e., $(M,K)$ is reduce to a Riemannian space.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $I^j=0$, so the space is Riemannian.

nodes.name: No non-Riemannian Einstein Cartan lift
nodes.statement: There is not exist any non-Riemannian Cartan structure such that $(T^{\ast}M_0, G, J)$ became a Einstein manifold.
conclusions: There is not exist any non-Riemannian Cartan structure such that $(T^{\ast}M_0, G, J)$ became a Einstein manifold.

nodes.name: Locally symmetric characterization
nodes.statement: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space of constant curvature $c$ and the components of the metric $G$ are given by (\ref{Kahler}). Then the following are hold if and only if $(M,K)$ is reduce to a Riemannian space.\\ $(i)$ for $c<0$, $(T^{\ast}M_0,G,J)$ is a locally symmetric K\"{a}hler manifold.\\ $(ii)$ for $c>0$, $(T_{\beta}^{\ast}M_0,G,J)$ is a locally symmetric K\"{a}hler manifold, where $T_{\beta}^{\ast}M_{\circ}$ is the tube around the zero section in $T^{\ast}M$, defined by the condition $2\tau<\frac{1}{c\beta^2}$.
assumptions: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space of constant curvature $c$ and the components of the metric $G$ are given by (\ref{Kahler}).
conclusions: the following are hold if and only if $(M,K)$ is reduce to a Riemannian space.
nodes.statement_short: The (tube in the) cotangent bundle with the Kähler metric is locally symmetric iff the Cartan space is Riemannian.
nodes.label: THM3

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.3
nodes.statement:
Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space. Using (ef{Curvature6}), (ef{curvature13})-(ef{curvature17}), we have computed the covariant derivatives of curvature tensor field $K$ in the local adapted frame $(\delta_i,\dot{\partial}^i)$ with respect to the connection $
abla$ and obtained in the twelve cases the result is zero. Conversely, let $(i)$ and $(ii)$ are hold. Thus we get $
abla K=0$. For simplify, we let $(M,K)$ be a Berwald-Cartan space. Put \[ (
abla K)({\dot{\partial}}^u,{\dot{\partial}}^i,\delta_j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=M^{uiks}_j\delta_s+N^{uik}_{sj}{\dot{\partial}}^s. \] Since $(
abla K)({\dot{\partial}}^u,{\dot{\partial}}^i,\delta_j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=0$, then we have $M^{uiks}_j=N^{uik}_{sj}=0$. Thus we have $p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=0$. By a straightforward calculation, we obtain  egin{eqnarray} p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=p^jp_iC^{ks,i,u}_j\!\!\!\!&-&\!\!\!\!2c eta	au(G^{ks,u}+G^{kh}C^{us}_h+G^{uh}C^{ks}_h+G^{hs}C^{uk}_h)
onumber\ \!\!\!\!&+&\!\!\!\! 2c^2 eta^2	au(G^{us}G^{kh}+G^{uk}G^{hs})p_h. \end{eqnarray} By a direct computation, we have  egin{equation} G^{ks,u}=-2 eta C^{ksu}+ rac{2c^2 eta^5}{(1-2c eta^2	au)^2}p^kp^up^s+ rac{c eta^3}{1-2c eta^2	au}g^{ku}p^s+ rac{c eta^3}{1-2c eta^2	au}g^{su}p^k. \end{equation} Also, we obtain  egin{equation} G^{us}G^{kh}p_h= rac{ eta}{1-2c eta^2	au}p^sG^{ku}= rac{ eta^2}{1-2c eta^2	au}g^{ku}p^s+ rac{c eta^4}{(1-2c eta^2	au)^2}p^up^kp^s, \end{equation} and  egin{equation} G^{uk}G^{hs}p_h= rac{ eta}{1-2c eta^2	au}p^kG^{su}= rac{ eta^2}{1-2c eta^2	au}g^{su}p^k+ rac{c eta^4}{(1-2c eta^2	au)^2}p^up^sp^k. \end{equation} Putting (ef{symmetric2}), (ef{symmetric3}) and (ef{symmetric4}) in (ef{symmetric1}), one can yields  egin{equation} p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=p^jp_iC^{ks,i,u}_j-2c eta	au(-2 eta C^{kus}+G^{kh}C^{us}_h+G^{uh}C^{ks}_h+G^{hs}C^{uk}_h). \end{equation} Since $p_iC^{ks,i}_j=-C^{ks}_j$, then we obtain \[ p^jp_iC^{ks,i,u}_j=2g^{uj}C^{ks}_j=2C^{kus}. \] Also, since $C^{us}_hp^h=0$, then we have \[ G^{kh}C^{us}_h=G^{uh}C^{ks}_h=G^{hs}C^{uk}_h= eta C^{kus}. \] Therefore (ef{symmetric5}) reduces to following  egin{equation} p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=2(1-c eta^2	au)C^{kus}. \end{equation} Since $p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=0$, then by (ef{symmetric6}), we have $C^{kus}=0$, i.e., $K$ is a Riemannian metric.
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction asserted by computing all components of $\nabla K$. Converse (for Berwald-Cartan spaces) contracts one component of $\nabla K=0$ to get $2(1-c\beta^2\tau)C^{kus}=0$.

nodes.name: Forward direction by computation
nodes.statement: Let $(M,K)$ be a Cartan space. Using (\ref{Curvature6}), (\ref{curvature13})-(\ref{curvature17}), we have computed the covariant derivatives of curvature tensor field $K$ in the local adapted frame $(\delta_i,\dot{\partial}^i)$ with respect to the connection $\nabla$ and obtained in the twelve cases the result is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Asserts the twelve components of $\nabla K$ vanish in the Riemannian case.

nodes.name: Converse setup
nodes.statement: Conversely, let $(i)$ and $(ii)$ are hold. Thus we get $\nabla K=0$.

nodes.name: Berwald-Cartan reduction
nodes.statement: For simplify, we let $(M,K)$ be a Berwald-Cartan space. Put \[ (\nabla K)({\dot{\partial}}^u,{\dot{\partial}}^i,\delta_j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=M^{uiks}_j\delta_s+N^{uik}_{sj}{\dot{\partial}}^s. \]
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to Berwald-Cartan spaces and name the components $M$, $N$ of one $\nabla K$ component.

nodes.name: Components vanish
nodes.statement: Since $(\nabla K)({\dot{\partial}}^u,{\dot{\partial}}^i,\delta_j,{\dot{\partial}}^k)=0$, then we have $M^{uiks}_j=N^{uik}_{sj}=0$. Thus we have $p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=0$.

nodes.name: Expand contraction
nodes.statement: By a straightforward calculation, we obtain \begin{eqnarray} p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=p^jp_iC^{ks,i,u}_j\!\!\!\!&-&\!\!\!\!2c\beta\tau(G^{ks,u}+G^{kh}C^{us}_h+G^{uh}C^{ks}_h+G^{hs}C^{uk}_h)\nonumber\\ \!\!\!\!&+&\!\!\!\! 2c^2\beta^2\tau(G^{us}G^{kh}+G^{uk}G^{hs})p_h. \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Compute G^{ks,u}
nodes.statement: By a direct computation, we have \begin{equation} G^{ks,u}=-2\beta C^{ksu}+\frac{2c^2\beta^5}{(1-2c\beta^2\tau)^2}p^kp^up^s+\frac{c\beta^3}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}g^{ku}p^s+\frac{c\beta^3}{1-2c\beta^2\tau}g^{su}p^k. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Substitute
nodes.statement: Putting (\ref{symmetric2}), (\ref{symmetric3}) and (\ref{symmetric4}) in (\ref{symmetric1}), one can yields \begin{equation} p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=p^jp_iC^{ks,i,u}_j-2c\beta\tau(-2\beta C^{kus}+G^{kh}C^{us}_h+G^{uh}C^{ks}_h+G^{hs}C^{uk}_h). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Contractions with C
nodes.statement: Also, since $C^{us}_hp^h=0$, then we have \[ G^{kh}C^{us}_h=G^{uh}C^{ks}_h=G^{hs}C^{uk}_h=\beta C^{kus}. \]

nodes.name: Conclude Riemannian
nodes.statement: Since $p^jp_iM^{uiks}_j=0$, then by (\ref{symmetric6}), we have $C^{kus}=0$, i.e., $K$ is a Riemannian metric.

nodes.name: No non-Riemannian locally symmetric Cartan lift
nodes.statement: There is not exist any non-Riemannian Cartan structure such that $(T^{\ast}M_0, G, J)$ became a locally symmetric manifold.
conclusions: There is not exist any non-Riemannian Cartan structure such that $(T^{\ast}M_0, G, J)$ became a locally symmetric manifold.
